desk_read: Yesterday's session was dominated by heavy expiry rolls and active positioning shifts across asset classes. Equity futures saw aggressive new buying, with the S&P 500 adding +54.9k contracts in total open interest alongside strong price gains. In contrast, energy markets like WTI Crude Oil and Natural Gas experienced declining total open interest alongside falling prices, driven by the expiry roll rather than directional flows. Precious metals showed a divergence between price and positioning, as Gold and Silver rallied sharply while total open interest fell by -15.3k and -5.8k contracts respectively, with the flow read pointing to short covering. Meanwhile, the Brent minus WTI spread stood at +9.20 $/bbl.

Brent (NYMEX) (BZG27) -3.64%, total open interest -2.7k (expiry roll), volume 0.8x the 20-day average; curve in backwardation, BZG27-BZH27 +2.20, BZG27-BZM27 +6.48 $/bbl (-0.42 vs previous session). Brent (NYMEX) minus WTI, same delivery month F27: +9.20 $/bbl.
bias_read: WTI Crude Oil shows a bias mildly bearish with volume 1.2x the 20-day average conviction, alongside a weakening curve in backwardation, while Brent displays a neutral bias with a weakening backwardated curve, though neither provides an open-interest reading to confirm follow-through. Meanwhile, S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100 present a bias mildly bullish driven by new longs and volume at 1.5x and 1.6x the 20-day average conviction respectively, where fresh positioning actively supports the current upward trend rather than warning of exhaustion. Gold mirrors this mildly bullish sentiment through short covering on volume 1.9x the 20-day average conviction, carrying a risk of a squeeze since closing positions are less durable. Overall, the short-term flow reveals a fractured picture with conviction backing equities while energy and metals reflect mixed signals.
